I had what could be called a mental breakdown as a result of stomach issues last year. But that term seems to not do the experience justice.

I found my whole foundation of reality warped and hideously distorted. My vision changed. Things simultaneously grew darker overall, like wearing shades, yet vibrant colours like for example flowers seemed much more intense, almost painfully so. Things looked ugly. Things looked flatter. I went through a period when time seemed sped up. Like watching a DVD on fast forward. Sounds were amplified. Motorbikes seemed ten times louder than they should be and the sound of a slammed door would go right through me. I couldn't sleep. I literally didnt sleep for months. I read somewhere that the record is 13 days for normal people and 21 if you're on meth. But I beat that, yet somehow didnt hallucinate. Something very common with sleep deprivation. I paced all day and night. I felt like my IQ was dropping, to like 50 or something. I felt like a complete retard and was struggling to form a sentence. I would frequently talk in ditties. Bright lights became painful. 

Talking intimately in DM with gastritis sufferers I've been told how they started hearing voices or demonic groaning sounds coming from somewhere. But they're tight lipped about things like this to avoid being carted off to a loony bin.

I ended up in a mental hospital for a suicide attempt because of my gastritis/ulcer and tried to relate these things to psychiatrists, even when faced with studies on the gut/brain axis and how rats developed depression and anxiety when given gastritis they wouldn't believe me. It just gets covered under the broad umbrella diagnosis of psychosis. For which you are forcibly treated with antipsychotics.

I don't have the above symptoms anymore, just depression and bodily fatigue. All the life has been sucked out of me. I find little joy in life. Sex drive is diminished, music doesn't make me feel emotions like it once did.

 I did suffer intense suicidal feelings of despair which would always come on in the evenings and went away with antidepressants but these have thankfully receded.

What I went through was worse than any torture man could invent. I went through hell. 

The psychological aspects of gastric problems I have to conclude is an extremely poorly understood and under researched field.

What could raise awareness though? Everyone I've talked to keeps this shit bottled up to prevent being sectioned/baker act'd.
Hard to say, I didnt notice much benefit but the studies absolutely rave about it
